Shriram. Corporate registry listings show a Prabha Shridhar as director of family-linked firms such as Prabha Shridhar Facilities Pvt Ltd. name: Jimmy William Almeida
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, G.M. Breweries Ltd (BSE 507488 / NSE GMBREW)
profile: Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap founded G.M. Breweries in Mumbai in 1981 and took it public in 1993. It is now Maharashtra's largest country-liquor maker, best known for its orange-flavoured G.M. Santra brand. He is still chairman and MD; shareholders reappointed him as MD through March 2028, and he owns a majority stake.
interesting_fact: G.M. Breweries started out bottling 200 cases a day. Its fully automatic plant at Virar, near Mumbai, can now turn out about 50,000 cases a day, and the company says it has paid a dividend every year since its 1993 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Country liquor used to be sold only in 750 ml and 375 ml bottles. According to the company, Almeida introduced the 180 ml bottle to the industry and was also the first to use PET (plastic) bottles for it.
notes: Low media profile. Filings use several name forms: Jimmy Almeida, Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap. The company secretary, Sandeep Kutchhi, is the formal contact route (https://www.gmbreweries.com/overview.html).

name: Zhou Xialong
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Young's China'. I could not find any public English-language source linking a 'Zhou Xialong' to a company of that name, so the identity is unresolved.
notes: Identity unresolved after several searches. The name may be a romanisation variant, and 'Young's China' may be a translated brand name. The Chinese characters for the name and company would be needed to research further.

name: Cheng Minghe
current_role: Co-founder and non-independent director, Shenzhen Mindray Bio-Medical Electronics (SZSE: 300760); renominated to the 9th board in April 2026
profile: Cheng Minghe co-founded Mindray in Shenzhen in 1991 with Li Xiting and Xu Hang, and built it into China's largest medical-device maker (patient monitors, ultrasound, in-vitro diagnostics). He ran sales, marketing and strategy, served as co-CEO from 2013, and was general manager from 2016 to 2020. He is still a director and a major shareholder.
interesting_fact: In February 2026 he gave about US$15 million (roughly RMB100 million) to his alma mater, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His total gifts there come to nearly RMB300 million and include 520 donated defibrillators (AEDs) and the Jiahe Health Innovation Building.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from a multi-generation Jiao Tong family: his parents both studied hoisting machinery at SJTU in the 1950s, and his maternal grandfather taught shipping management there in 1950. As a biomedical-instrumentation student (class of 1985), he spent a year at the medical school taking more than 30 courses and doing clinical rotations.
notes: Name also romanised as Minghe Cheng or Ming He Cheng. He keeps a low international media profile. Possible angles for outreach are his SJTU philanthropy (the Jiahe Fund) and medical-engineering integration.

name: Deep Kalra
current_role: Founder, Group Chairman & Chief Mentor, MakeMyTrip (NASDAQ: MMYT)
profile: Deep Kalra founded MakeMyTrip in 2000 after stints at ABN AMRO, AMF Bowling and GE Capital, and built it into India's largest online travel company, which listed on Nasdaq in 2010. He handed day-to-day leadership to Group CEO Rajesh Magow and in 2022 became group chairman and chief mentor. He also co-founded Ashoka University and chaired the WTTC India Initiative from 2024 to 2026.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for MakeMyTrip while trying to sell his wife's car online, which showed him what the internet could do for transactions in India.
deep_cut_fact: Before MakeMyTrip, after IIM Ahmedabad and three years at ABN AMRO, he worked with AMF Bowling setting up bowling alleys in India. He then joined GE Capital as VP of business development in 1999.
notes: The IR email is the company's published investor-relations contact (Vipul Garg, SVP IR), not Kalra's own. He speaks publicly a lot on travel, startups and philanthropy, including Ashoka University and the 'I am Gurgaon' NGO.

name: Frederick R Wilson
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, Union Square Ventures (New York); former director of Coinbase and Etsy
profile: Fred Wilson has been a venture capitalist since 1986. He co-founded Flatiron Partners and, in 2003, Union Square Ventures, which made early bets on Twitter, Tumblr, Etsy, Coinbase, Zynga and Kickstarter. He has served on the boards of Etsy and Coinbase. He has blogged almost daily at AVC.com since September 2003.
interesting_fact: His blog AVC has run since September 2003, mostly every weekday. He calls it a public diary where he works through ideas, and it is one of the longest-running VC blogs.
deep_cut_fact: He helped launch the Academy for Software Engineering, a non-selective New York City public high school that opened in 2012. The idea was a shared dream with Stuyvesant CS teacher Mike Zamansky, and his CSNYC effort helped shape the city's later CS4All program.
notes: Very accessible online through AVC (posts and comments) and X. He writes about climate and energy as well as crypto, which makes a good hook. USV has climate-focused investment theses.

name: Robert L. Goldstein
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, BlackRock, Inc.; oversees Aladdin and the firm's operating and technology platforms
profile: Rob Goldstein joined BlackRock in 1994 at age 20, straight out of Binghamton University (BS economics), and has spent his whole career there. He helped build BlackRock Solutions and the Aladdin risk and portfolio platform, ran the institutional client business from 2012, and became COO in 2014. He sits on the Global Executive Committee and leads the firm's technology and AI agenda.
interesting_fact: When he joined, BlackRock had about 55 employees. It now manages more than $10 trillion. In 2024 he said generative AI would be 'the most significant technology, innovation, evolution, revolution' of his 30-year career.
deep_cut_fact: He started in BlackRock's Portfolio Analytics Group and was part of the BlackRock Solutions technology unit from its early days. He worked under Charles Hallac, Aladdin's architect, and Institutional Investor repeatedly named him to its Tech 50 list (2013-2017).
notes: BlackRock media relations contact is Patrick Scanlan (212-810-3622), per the Q2 2026 earnings release (https://s24.q4cdn.com/856567660/files/doc_financials/2026/Q2/BLK-2Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf). Strong data-center angle: BlackRock's GIP/AIP AI infrastructure partnership, plus Aladdin and AI. Go through BlackRock corporate communications.

name: Wang Aihua
current_role: Chief Technology Officer, TOYO Co., Ltd / VSUN (Nasdaq: TOYO), a Japan-headquartered solar cell and module maker with factories in Vietnam
profile: Dr. Aihua Wang is a UNSW-trained photovoltaic scientist. With her husband Dr. Jianhua Zhao she co-founded China Sunergy / CEEG (Nanjing) PV-Tech in 2006, in which she held equity, and led its R&D as head of research and VP. She became CTO of VSUN/TOYO in 2024 and in 2026 presented on solar power in space to investors.
interesting_fact: In 2023 she, Jianhua Zhao, Martin Green and Andrew Blakers received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering for developing PERC solar cell technology, which now dominates global solar production.
deep_cut_fact: Working in Martin Green's UNSW lab, she and Zhao set several world records for silicon solar cell efficiency, including the 25.0% PERL cell. In 2013 she won the ACAA/IELTS Australia China Alumni Award for Research and Innovation.
notes: An excellent energy-podcast fit as a world-class PV scientist. The listed wealth source 'CEEG PV-Tech' refers to her early equity in China Sunergy (controlled by Lu Tingxiu's CEEG). Her husband Jianhua Zhao is VSUN group chief advisor. Best route is TOYO investor relations.

name: Richard M McVey
current_role: Founder and former CEO/Executive Chairman of MarketAxess (retired end of 2024); Miami University (OH) trustee; senior advisor to an AI data company
profile: Rick McVey incubated MarketAxess inside J.P. Morgan in 1999 while running North American fixed-income sales, and spun it out in 2000. He built it into the leading electronic corporate-bond trading platform and ran it as CEO until 2023. He was executive chairman through 2024 and then retired. He now focuses on philanthropy, board work and advising an AI firm that builds datasets for illiquid assets.
interesting_fact: When MarketAxess spun out of J.P. Morgan in January 2000, around 50 other electronic bond-trading startups were competing. McVey recalls that the hardest early hurdle was client onboarding, which was 'arduous and painfully slow with the legal reviews.'
deep_cut_fact: A Miami University class of 1981 alumnus, he gave $20 million for the 87,000 sq ft Richard M. McVey Data Science Building on Miami's Oxford, Ohio campus, one of the five largest single gifts in the school's history. He also funded the McVey Center for Computational and Data Sciences at Colby College.
notes: Retired from MarketAxess at the end of 2024, so the SEC 'Executive Chairman' tag is outdated. He has no public personal channels that I found. Possible routes are Miami University (as a trustee) or MarketAxess corporate communications. He is interested in AI and data science.

name: Jay J Jackson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Abacus Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: ABX; formerly Abacus Life, Nasdaq: ABL), Orlando
profile: Jay Jackson is a life-settlements and longevity-finance specialist. He started at Franklin Templeton, co-founded Abacus Life Settlements in 2004, and ran the Fayerweather Street Life Fund and the Cambridge Life Management platform for Ken Froot's FDO Partners. He has led Abacus since 2016, took it public in 2023, and has expanded it into asset management, longevity data (Abacus Intel) and wealth advisory.
interesting_fact: According to Abacus, its life-settlements business has transacted more than $10 billion in face value of life insurance policies, buying policies from seniors and managing them as an alternative asset class tied to longevity.
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he sits on the Orlando Mayor's Committee on Livability and is an executive board member of the Senior Resource Alliance, an agency of the Florida Department of Elder Affairs.
notes: Media-friendly: he has spoken at Milken 2026 and on ICR's podcast. press@abacusgm.com is the best route.

name: Michael N. Kennedy
current_role: CEO and President, Antero Resources (NYSE: AR) and Antero Midstream (NYSE: AM), Denver
profile: Michael Kennedy runs Antero Resources, one of the largest US natural gas and NGL producers in the Appalachian Basin, and its midstream affiliate. He joined Antero in 2013, was CFO of Antero Resources from 2021 to 2025, and then became CEO of both companies. Before Antero he was EVP and CFO of Forest Oil (2009-2013).
interesting_fact: Antero is a major Appalachian natural-gas supplier at a time when US gas demand is growing with LNG exports and power for AI data centers, which makes Kennedy a relevant voice on gas-for-data-center supply.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an Arthur Andersen auditor focused on the natural-resources industry, joined Forest Oil in 2001 in finance roles, and rose to its EVP and CFO by 2009. He holds an accounting degree from the University of Colorado Boulder.
notes: The IR email belongs to Dan Katzenberg, VP Investor Relations, as published on Antero's investor page. Strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast (Appalachian gas and data-center power demand). The SEC 'See Remarks' tag reflects his move from CFO to CEO.
